A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Cost-aware Stopping for Bayesian Optimization by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, table, and Appendices A–D are readable and support matching retained content across revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gaussian-process simulations, LCBench hyperparameter-optimization experiments, NATS-Bench architecture-search experiments, and runtime and stopping-behavior analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and reports expanded evaluation across all 35 LCBench datasets, including aggregate and per-dataset results.

M1.justification: The proposed after-posterior-update stopping rule and PBGI/LogEIPC acquisition definitions remain unchanged in Equations (4)–(10). The theoretical corrections and expanded experimental documentation do not establish a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: LCBench evaluation expands from Fashion-MNIST, adult, and higgs to all 35 datasets, substantially broadening the represented classification problems and dataset sizes. The synthetic scenarios and three NATS-Bench datasets are retained.

E2.justification: The comparator roster is otherwise retained, but v2 Figure 19 labels the unknown-cost acquisition LogEIPC-exp, whereas v4 Figure 18 labels it LogEIPC-inv and changes some plotted entries. v4's caption and Appendix D.3 still specify LogEIPC-exp and expected-cost substitution, leaving actual comparator replacement unresolved.

E3.justification: v4 adds min–max normalization across acquisition–stopping pairs for aggregate LCBench evaluation and dataset-specific regression slopes for the full benchmark's runtime proxies. The original three-dataset 0.001-times-parameter-count setup remains in the appendix; initialization and iteration budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix D.3 adds failure and sensitivity analysis distinguishing seven datasets with persistent underperformance across all three cost scales from three that recover at the smallest scale. Existing posterior-update, smoothing, runtime, and cost-mismatch analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 50 random seeds and means with error bars of twice the standard error. Added plots and changed error-bar values do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice or statistical testing procedure.

E6.justification: v4 adds aggregate and per-dataset results for the full LCBench benchmark at three cost scales, reporting competitive matched-pair performance on roughly 75% of datasets and identifying persistent failures. Some unknown-cost LogEIPC entries also change, with variant ambiguity preventing direct performance attribution. Table 1 and the retained synthetic appendix curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: Lemma 1 generalizes the constant prior mean to a mean function and corrects the expected-improvement time indexing. Appendix B replaces the optional-stopping invocation with an explicit indicator/tower-property calculation and completes the regret-plus-cost bound. New Corollary 3 proves high-probability finite termination under a positive cost floor; the previous budget-scaling corollary is retained as Corollary 4.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions broaden the empirical recommendation from pairing the rule with PBGI to pairing it with PBGI or LogEIPC. The introduction also explicitly frames applicability to classical and cost-aware Bayesian optimization. The central stopping-rule contribution remains the same.

C2.justification: v4 adds the hypothesis that small datasets contribute to model misspecification and poor performance, while acknowledging two larger-dataset exceptions. It also explicitly states that the matched stopping rationale does not automatically extend to KG or MES. v2's general model-mismatch discussion and NATS failure interpretation are retained.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-repository link on the first page, documents regression-based runtime proxies for the full LCBench evaluation, and clarifies that 20-iteration averaging applies to all acquisition-value-based stopping rules. These are additions to access and implementation information, without establishing reruns of retained experiments.

R1.justification: v4 adds the OpenML reference by Vanschoren et al. and sharpens the connection to Nguyen et al.'s existing EI stopping rule and the distinction from other acquisition-design principles. The broader Pandora's Box and PBGI positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution paragraphs are rewritten, acquisition definitions receive clearer explanations, and the stopping-rule taxonomy changes from a numbered list to paragraph headings. Cross-references and terminology are refined, while the overall section and appendix organization remains stable.

P2.justification: v4 merges the separate 1D and 8D main-text plots into Figure 2, replaces the main LCBench panels with aggregate comparisons, and adds three full-page grids covering 35 datasets with failure highlighting. Retained appendix plots are relocated and regrouped; these are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v4 repairs indexing and completes the proof of the central regret guarantee, adds a finite-termination guarantee, and substantially broadens empirical validation while documenting failure cases. These changes strengthen mathematical support and clarify applicability beyond v2's narrow LCBench evaluation. The unresolved LogEIPC-exp/inv inconsistency in one auxiliary figure limits that comparison but does not outweigh the gains.
